findings.evidence: The `.qr` container that hosts the injected QR `<svg>` (borne.blade.php:414, validation.blade.php:138) carries no `role="img"`/`aria-label`/`<title>`, unlike the wheel canvas on the SAME borne screen which does (`<canvas class="roue" ... role="img" aria-label="Roue des lots: ...">`, borne.blade.php:342-343) — an inconsistent a11y pattern within one file. INVESTIGATED, not a blank hole in practice: (1) inline SVG with no focusable descendants and no accessible-name source is excluded from the accessibility tree by Chromium — a screen reader will silently skip it, not read raw path data; (2) the adjacent visible copy already conveys the QR's purpose without a formal aria association — borne: "Scanne avec ton téléphone / Aucune application à installer"; validation: "À lui de tourner / Fais-lui scanner ce QR maintenant, devant toi" (both confirmed present in the .dom.html snapshots). The `.qr-logo img alt=""` decorative choice (borne.blade.php:233-234 comment) is correct and is NOT the gap — the gap, if any, is the unlabeled SVG wrapper, and it is covered by surrounding prose, not left blank.
findings.fix_hint: Optional robustness improvement, not a regression: add `role="img" aria-label="QR code — {{ scan instruction }}"` to `.qr` in borne.blade.php:414 and validation.blade.php:138, mirroring the existing `.roue` canvas pattern, so the accessible name is explicit rather than relying on DOM-order proximity to unassociated text.

verification_notes.spec_rerun: Re-ran tests/e2e/roue-qr-logo-2026-08-13.spec.js live (chromium, workers=1, retries=0) from a clean rate-limit window: 4/4 passed, matching the GStack report. Also independently re-ran tests/e2e/roue-2026-08-13.spec.js: 9/9 passed on a clean run (a same-session earlier attempt showed 1 failure at ouvrirLaPorte() — traced to MY OWN prior test runs having consumed the 5-attempts/min/IP wheel-pin rate limit, per RouteServiceProvider.php `wheel-pin` limiter; not a real regression, confirmed by rerunning after the window cleared).
verification_notes.decode_authenticity: Confirmed the spec decodes the actual rendered browser artifact, not the controller's raw SVG string: `page.locator('.qr-boite'|'.qr').screenshot({path: cropPath})` writes a real PNG, then `decode-qr.php` runs `Zxing\QrReader` (GD mode) against that PNG file. Not a shortcut/cheat.
verification_notes.dpr2_claim: Verified by direct reproduction, not by trusting the code comment: duplicated the spec with deviceScaleFactor forced to 1 and reran against a scratch captures dir. Result: the two borne screens (larger QR) still decoded fine at DPR:1, but the validation screen's smaller 260px-CSS QR genuinely failed to decode ('decode-qr: aucun QR décodable dans ...03-validation-issue-1.qr-crop.png') — exactly the failure mode described in the spec's comment (roue-qr-logo-2026-08-13.spec.js:159-167). The DPR:2/Retina justification is real, not pretext for hiding a fragile decode.
verification_notes.token_leak_check: Grepped all 4 .dom.html snapshots for a `t=<token>` pattern and for the exact token strings returned by decode: zero matches. `.lien` text content is exactly 'www.lecayenne.fr — scanne le QR ci-dessus' (domain-only, via PHP_URL_HOST per the 2026-08-09 fix) on both validation captures, confirmed independently of the spec's own assertion.
verification_notes.visual_review: Opened all 4 full-page PNGs and all 4 .qr-crop.png crops with vision. Logo disc is visually centered, adequate white-background contrast against the QR modules, not pixelated at either capture size (776x776 down to 584x584, both already 2x DPR). No layout shift/overlap from the label-sizing fix (73d34ae84) — wheel segment labels (Cheese Burger, Cayenne, Terminator, Tarte Daim, Tiramisu, Frites, Boisson) render at one uniform size in both orientations, matching the fix's stated intent and its file-scoped diff (borne.blade.php only, +21 lines, no unrelated changes).
